source: For now, our typical (or median) 11-year-old wears a size 9 in the junior’s section
claim: The median waistline of girls aged 10–11 is 27.27 inches, nearest the 27.48-inch waist of a junior size 9 (0.21 inches away).
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age in ['10','11'] and race=='all'").assign(percent50=lambda d: d.percent50.astype(float), w=lambda d: d.participants.str.replace(',','').astype(int)).groupby('yearRange').apply(lambda d: np.average(d.percent50, weights=d.w), include_groups=False).to_frame('v').reset_index()[['v']].merge(astm.query("sizeRange=='junior'")[['size','waist']], how='cross').assign(diff=lambda d: (d.waist-d.v).abs()).nsmallest(1,'diff')

claim: The median waistline of girls aged 14–15 is 30.37 inches.
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age in ['14','15'] and race=='all'").assign(percent50=lambda d: d.percent50.astype(float), w=lambda d: d.participants.str.replace(',','').astype(int)).groupby('yearRange').apply(lambda d: np.average(d.percent50, weights=d.w), include_groups=False).to_frame('v').reset_index()

source: Here, the median 15-year-old’s waistline fits a size 10
claim: The median waistline of girls aged 14–15 is 30.37 inches, nearest the 30.5-inch waist of a size 10 (0.13 inches away).
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age in ['14','15'] and race=='all'").assign(percent50=lambda d: d.percent50.astype(float), w=lambda d: d.participants.str.replace(',','').astype(int)).groupby('yearRange').apply(lambda d: np.average(d.percent50, weights=d.w), include_groups=False).to_frame('v').reset_index()[['v']].merge(astm.query("year==2021 and sizeRange=='straight'")[['size','alphaSize','waist']], how='cross').assign(diff=lambda d: (d.waist-d.v).abs()).nsmallest(1,'diff')

source: The median 15-year-old wears a Medium, as she has throughout most of her childhood.
claim: The ASTM size nearest the 30.37-inch median waistline of girls aged 14–15 is a size 10, labeled M.
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age in ['14','15'] and race=='all'").assign(percent50=lambda d: d.percent50.astype(float), w=lambda d: d.participants.str.replace(',','').astype(int)).groupby('yearRange').apply(lambda d: np.average(d.percent50, weights=d.w), include_groups=False).to_frame('v').reset_index()[['v']].merge(astm.query("year==2021 and sizeRange=='straight'")[['size','alphaSize','waist']], how='cross').assign(diff=lambda d: (d.waist-d.v).abs()).nsmallest(1,'diff')

source: Girls who fall along the bottom 10th percentile can now wear an Extra Small in women’s clothing
claim: The 10th-percentile waistline of girls aged 14–15 is 26.97 inches, nearest the 26.88-inch waist of a size 2, labeled XS.
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age in ['14','15'] and race=='all'").assign(percent10=lambda d: d.percent10.astype(float), w=lambda d: d.participants.str.replace(',','').astype(int)).groupby('yearRange').apply(lambda d: np.average(d.percent10, weights=d.w), include_groups=False).to_frame('v').reset_index()[['v']].merge(astm.query("year==2021 and sizeRange=='straight'")[['size','alphaSize','waist']], how='cross').assign(diff=lambda d: (d.waist-d.v).abs()).nsmallest(1,'diff')

source: while girls near the 90th percentile will find that an Extra Large generally fits.
claim: The 90th-percentile waistline of girls aged 14–15 is 38.18 inches, nearest the 38.25-inch waist of a size 18, labeled XL.
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age in ['14','15'] and race=='all'").assign(percent90=lambda d: d.percent90.astype(float), w=lambda d: d.participants.str.replace(',','').astype(int)).groupby('yearRange').apply(lambda d: np.average(d.percent90, weights=d.w), include_groups=False).to_frame('v').reset_index()[['v']].merge(astm.query("year==2021 and sizeRange=='straight'")[['size','alphaSize','waist']], how='cross').assign(diff=lambda d: (d.waist-d.v).abs()).nsmallest(1,'diff')

source: Altogether, the median adult woman over the age of 20 fits a size 18.
claim: The median waistline of women 20 and over is 37.96 inches, nearest the 38.25-inch waist of a size 18 (0.29 inches away).
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age=='20 and over' and race=='all'")[['percent50']].astype(float).merge(astm.query("year==2021 and sizeRange=='straight'")[['size','alphaSize','waist']], how='cross').assign(diff=lambda d: (d.waist-d.percent50).abs()).nsmallest(1,'diff')

source: At this point the median woman is closer to a size 16 or Extra Large.
claim: The median waistline of women aged 30–39 is 37.09 inches, nearest the 36.0-inch waist of a size 16, labeled XL (1.09 inches away).
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age=='30–39' and race=='all'")[['percent50']].astype(float).merge(astm.query("year==2021 and sizeRange=='straight'")[['size','alphaSize','waist']], how='cross').assign(diff=lambda d: (d.waist-d.percent50).abs()).nsmallest(1,'diff')

source: That leaves millions of people — over half of all adult women — who are excluded from standard size ranges.
claim: The median waistline of women 20 and over, 37.96 inches, is 1.96 inches above the 36.0-inch waist of a size 16, so more than half of adult women are above the top of the standard straight range.
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age=='20 and over' and race=='all'")[['percent50']].astype(float).merge(astm.query("year==2021 and sizeRange=='straight' and size==16")[['waist']], how='cross').assign(above=lambda d: d.percent50-d.waist)

source: According to U.S. health data, fewer than 10% of adult women have waistlines that fit the standard sample size or smaller.
claim: The 10th-percentile waistline of women 20 and over, 30.36 inches, is 0.86 inches above the 29.5-inch waist of a size 8, so fewer than 10% of adult women have waistlines that fit the standard sample size or smaller.
code: waist.query("yearRange=='2015-2018' and age=='20 and over' and race=='all'")[['percent10']].astype(float).merge(astm.query("year==2021 and sizeRange=='straight' and size==8")[['waist']], how='cross').assign(above=lambda d: d.percent10-d.waist)

source: Roughly 30 years ago, ASTM guidelines covered waistlines between 24 and 36.5 inches, representing a 12.5-inch spread from size 2–20.
claim: The 1995 ASTM straight chart runs from size 2 at 24.0 inches to size 20 at 36.5 inches, a 12.5-inch spread.

source: ASTM guidelines span 15.12 inches from 25.38–40.5 inches for sizes 00–20.
claim: The twelve waist measurements in the 2021 ASTM straight chart span 15.12 inches, from 25.38 to 40.5 inches.

source: By comparison, today’s size 8 is 2.5 inches larger in the waist than it was 30 years ago.
claim: The waist of a size 8 is 29.5 inches in the 2021 ASTM chart against 27.0 inches in 1995, 2.5 inches larger.

source: Today, because of vanity sizing, we can see an upward shift in all sizes.
claim: All ten sizes shared by the 1995 and 2021 ASTM straight charts are larger in 2021: size 2 rises from 24.0 to 26.88 inches and size 20 from 36.5 to 40.5 inches.
code: astm.query("sizeRange=='straight' and year in [1995,2021]").pivot_table(index='size', columns='year', values='waist').dropna().assign(growth=lambda d: d[2021]-d[1995])

source: In the early 2000s ASTM added size 00 and 0 to pad out the bottom of the range.
claim: The 1995 and 2001 ASTM straight charts run from size 2 to 20 with 10 sizes, while the 2011 and 2021 charts run from size 0 (the 00 and 0 sizes) to 20 with 12 sizes.

source: The average woman’s waistline today is nearly 4 inches wider than it was in the mid-1990s.
claim: The mean waistline of women 20 and over is 38.75 inches in 2015–2018 against 34.88 inches in 1988–1994, 3.87 inches wider.
code: waist.query("yearRange in ['1988-1994','2015-2018'] and age=='20 and over' and race=='all'").set_index('yearRange')['mean'].to_frame().sort_index().assign(growth=lambda d: d['mean'].diff())
